addition of commercial paper with a maturity of over three months of $<a name="XBRL_CS_ed0923bfafcf4589bceb1d4db"></a>5.3<a name="XBRL_CS_ed0923bfafcf4589bceb1d4db_bclEnd"></a> billion in 2019 and a net
reduction of $<a name="XBRL_CS_7b36482626d94f7d8777b1886"></a>0.3<a name="XBRL_CS_7b36482626d94f7d8777b1886_bclEnd"></a> billion in 2018. The gross
amount of commercial paper with a maturity of over three months issued was $<a name="XBRL_CS_d382b62f11674daea92005c93"></a>6.4<a name="XBRL_CS_d382b62f11674daea92005c93_bclEnd"></a> billion in 2019 and $<a name="XBRL_CS_288d871f5541488497822a67b"></a>0.4<a name="XBRL_CS_288d871f5541488497822a67b_bclEnd"></a> billion in 2018, while the
gross amount repaid was $<a name="XBRL_CS_479dfb984f6c43bda106982cd"></a>1.1<a name="XBRL_CS_479dfb984f6c43bda106982cd_bclEnd"></a> billion in 2019 and $<a name="XBRL_CS_b997a02e17d24520a61cc44b3"></a>0.7<a name="XBRL_CS_b997a02e17d24520a61cc44b3_bclEnd"></a> billion in 2018.<a name="XBRL_FS_d9731230ff0e4afcba5b41f85_bclEnd"></a></font></i></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;mso-border-shadow:yes;mso-line-height-rule:exactly;mso-padding-alt:31.0pt 31.0pt 31.0pt 31.0pt;mso-pagination:widow-orphan no-line-numbers;"><font style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:.7pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>


</DIV>
<p align=center style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-right:0pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">EXXON MOBIL CORPORATION</font></b></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-right:.1in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-right:.1in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">NOTES TO CONDENSED
CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></b></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.25in;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.25in;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><a name="XBRL_CS_b363b2e96ae54524abba64b56"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">1.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Basis of Financial Statement Preparation</font></b></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.25in;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">These unaudited condensed consolidated
financial statements should be read in the context of the consolidated
financial statements and notes thereto filed with the Securities and Exchange
Commission in the Corporation's 2018 Annual Report on Form 10-K. In the opinion
of the Corporation, the information furnished herein reflects all known
accruals and adjustments necessary for a fair statement of the results for the
periods reported herein. All such adjustments are of a normal recurring nature.
Prior data has been reclassified in certain cases to conform to the current
presentation basis.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Corporation's exploration and
production activities are accounted for under the &quot;successful
efforts&quot; method.</font></font><a name="XBRL_CS_b363b2e96ae54524abba64b56_bclEnd"></a></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"><br>
<br>
</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><a name="XBRL_TS_ed6e068116d24f30a96156018"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">2.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Accounting Changes</font></b></font><a name="XBRL_TS_ed6e068116d24f30a96156018_bclEnd"></a></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><a name="XBRL_TS_b9b137bc91864c80a40ad49cf"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Effective January 1, 2019, the Corporation adopted the Financial
Accounting Standards Board&#8217;s Standard, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Leases (Topic 842)</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, as amended.
The standard requires all leases to be recorded on the balance sheet as a right
of use asset and a lease liability. The Corporation used a transition method
that applies the new lease standard at January 1, 2019. </font></font><a name="XBRL_TS_51a7b0f41d074b59a4000f8c0"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Corporation applied a policy election to exclude short-term
leases from balance sheet recognition and also elected certain practical
expedients at adoption. As permitted, the Corporation did not reassess whether
existing contracts are or contain leases, the lease classification for any
existing leases, initial direct costs for any existing lease and whether
existing land easements and rights of way, which were not previously accounted
for as leases, are or contain a lease.</font></font><a name="XBRL_TS_51a7b0f41d074b59a4000f8c0_bclEnd"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> At adoption on January 1, 2019, an
operating lease liability of $<a name="XBRL_CS_9cec9bef069047d2990c5f0c9"></a>3.3<a name="XBRL_CS_9cec9bef069047d2990c5f0c9_bclEnd"></a> billion was recorded and
the operating lease right of use asset was $<a name="XBRL_CS_d76490fbaa4848a8acb886c06"></a>4.3<a name="XBRL_CS_d76490fbaa4848a8acb886c06_bclEnd"></a> billion, including $<a name="XBRL_CS_c61637f12e51445fbf63f69d8"></a>1.0<a name="XBRL_CS_c61637f12e51445fbf63f69d8_bclEnd"></a> billion of previously
recorded prepaid leases. There was no cumulative earnings effect adjustment.</font></font><a name="XBRL_TS_b9b137bc91864c80a40ad49cf_bclEnd"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> &nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><a name="XBRL_TS_5b27254a80a24c5ab7a24ea93"></a><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Effective January 1, 2020, ExxonMobil will adopt the Financial
Accounting Standards Board&#8217;s update, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financial Instruments &#8211; Credit Losses
(Topic 326)</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, as amended. The standard requires a valuation allowance for
credit losses be recognized for certain financial assets that reflects the
current expected credit loss over the asset&#8217;s contractual life. The valuation
allowance considers the risk of loss, even if remote, and considers past
events, current conditions and expectations of the future. The Corporation is
evaluating the standard and its effect on the Corporation&#8217;s financial
statements.</font></font><a name="XBRL_TS_5b27254a80a24c5ab7a24ea93_bclEnd"></a></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"><br>
<br>
</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><a name="XBRL_CS_3a9df1fe8b7a4a1ea5785dd07"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">3.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Litigation and Other Contingencies</font></b></font><a name="XBRL_CS_3a9df1fe8b7a4a1ea5785dd07_bclEnd"></a></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-right:0pt;"><a name="XBRL_CS_c49ceb4b457b47dfab3448b5c"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Litigation</font></b></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-right:0pt;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">A variety of claims
have been made against ExxonMobil and certain of its consolidated subsidiaries
in a number of pending lawsuits. Management has regular litigation reviews, including
updates from corporate and outside counsel, to assess the need for accounting
recognition or disclosure of these contingencies. The Corporation accrues an
undiscounted liability for those contingencies where the incurrence of a loss
is probable and the amount can be reasonably estimated. If a range of amounts
can be reasonably estimated and no amount within the range is a better estimate
than any other amount, then the minimum of the range is accrued. The
Corporation does not record liabilities when the likelihood that the liability
has been incurred is probable but the amount cannot be reasonably estimated or
when the liability is believed to be only reasonably possible or remote. For
contingencies where an unfavorable outcome is reasonably possible and which are
significant, the Corporation discloses the nature of the contingency and, where
feasible, an estimate of the possible loss. For purposes of our contingency
disclosures, &#8220;significant&#8221; includes material matters, as well as other matters
which management believes should be disclosed. ExxonMobil will continue to
defend itself vigorously in these matters. Based on a consideration of all
relevant facts and circumstances, the Corporation does not believe the ultimate
outcome of any currently pending lawsuit against ExxonMobil will have a
material adverse effect upon the Corporation's operations, financial condition,
or financial statements taken as a whole.</font></font><a name="XBRL_CS_c49ceb4b457b47dfab3448b5c_bclEnd"></a></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><a name="XBRL_CS_84d6e47c59314f068b5e0cc82"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other Contingencies</font></b></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:6.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Corporation and
certain of its consolidated subsidiaries were contingently liable at
March&nbsp;31, 2019, for guarantees relating to notes, loans and performance
under contracts. Where guarantees for environmental remediation and other
similar matters do not include a stated cap, the amounts reflect management&#8217;s
estimate of the maximum potential exposure. These guarantees are not reasonably
likely to have a material effect on the Corporation&#8217;s financial condition,
changes in financial condition, revenues or expenses, results of operations,
liquidity, capital expenditures or capital resources.</font></font><a name="XBRL_CS_84d6e47c59314f068b5e0cc82_bclEnd"></a></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><a name="XBRL_TS_99f00952120240018560dfde5"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Additionally, the Corporation and its affiliates have numerous
long-term sales and purchase commitments in their various business activities,
all of which are expected to be fulfilled with no adverse consequences material
to the Corporation&#8217;s operations or financial condition.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:8.0pt;text-align:justify;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
operations and earnings of the Corporation and its affiliates throughout the
world have been, and may in the future be, affected from time to time in varying
degree by political developments and laws and regulations, such as forced
divestiture of assets; restrictions on production, imports and exports; price
controls; tax increases and retroactive tax claims; expropriation of property;
cancellation of contract rights and environmental regulations. Both the
likelihood of such occurrences and their overall effect upon the Corporation
vary greatly from country to country and are not predictable.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In accordance with a
Venezuelan nationalization decree issued in February 2007, a subsidiary of the
Venezuelan National Oil Company (PdVSA) assumed the operatorship of the Cerro
Negro Heavy Oil Project. The decree also required conversion of the Cerro Negro
Project into a &#8220;mixed enterprise&#8221; and an increase in PdVSA&#8217;s or one of its
affiliate&#8217;s ownership interest in the Project. ExxonMobil refused to accede to
the terms proffered by the government, and on June 27, 2007, the government
expropriated ExxonMobil&#8217;s <a name="XBRL_CS_64c83f30194c4a94aeb0d7089"></a>41.67<a name="XBRL_CS_64c83f30194c4a94aeb0d7089_bclEnd"></a> percent interest in the
Cerro Negro Project.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">ExxonMobil collected
awards of $<a name="XBRL_CS_212b958727254f7589bd7db4b"></a>908<a name="XBRL_CS_212b958727254f7589bd7db4b_bclEnd"></a> million in an arbitration
against PdVSA under the rules of the International Chamber of Commerce in
respect of an indemnity related to the Cerro Negro Project and $<a name="XBRL_CS_dbf984b579d24dd8ba20be483"></a>260<a name="XBRL_CS_dbf984b579d24dd8ba20be483_bclEnd"></a> million in an arbitration
for compensation due for the La Ceiba Project and for export curtailments at
the Cerro Negro Project under rules of International Centre for Settlement of
Investment Disputes (ICSID). An ICSID arbitration award relating to the Cerro
Negro Project&#8217;s expropriation ($<a name="XBRL_CS_c49d42e23aba425bbb545182c"></a>1.4<a name="XBRL_CS_c49d42e23aba425bbb545182c_bclEnd"></a> billion) was annulled
based on a determination that a prior Tribunal failed to adequately explain why
the cap on damages in the indemnity owed by PdVSA did not affect or limit the
amount owed for the expropriation of the Cerro Negro Project. ExxonMobil filed
a new claim seeking to restore the original award of damages for the Cerro
Negro Project with ICSID on September 26, 2018.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The net impact of this
matter on the Corporation&#8217;s consolidated financial results cannot be reasonably
estimated. Regardless, the Corporation does not expect the resolution to have a
material effect upon the Corporation&#8217;s operations or financial condition.</font></font><a name="XBRL_TS_99f00952120240018560dfde5_bclEnd"></a></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><a name="XBRL_TS_f4348cf8394e4381bc24c5eaa"></a><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">An affiliate of ExxonMobil is one of the Contractors
under a Production Sharing Contract (PSC) with the Nigerian National Petroleum
Corporation (NNPC) covering the Erha block located in the offshore waters of
Nigeria. ExxonMobil's affiliate is the operator of the block and owns a </font></font><a name="XBRL_CS_d658be81a44d40d7a29d08602"></a><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">56.25</font></font><a name="XBRL_CS_d658be81a44d40d7a29d08602_bclEnd"></a><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> percent interest under the
PSC. The Contractors are in dispute with NNPC regarding NNPC's lifting of crude
oil in excess of its entitlement under the terms of the PSC. In accordance with
the terms of the PSC, the Contractors initiated arbitration in Abuja, Nigeria,
under the Nigerian Arbitration and Conciliation Act. On October&nbsp;24, 2011, a
three-member arbitral Tribunal issued an award upholding the Contractors'
position in all material respects and awarding damages to the Contractors
jointly in an amount of approximately $<a name="XBRL_CS_5af39e93ecc14cb499234366d"></a>1.8<a name="XBRL_CS_5af39e93ecc14cb499234366d_bclEnd"></a> billion plus $<a name="XBRL_CS_4f73422e88a94106bfeac2286"></a>234<a name="XBRL_CS_4f73422e88a94106bfeac2286_bclEnd"></a> million in accrued
interest. The Contractors petitioned a Nigerian federal court for enforcement
of the award, and NNPC petitioned the same court to have the award set aside.
On May&nbsp;22, 2012, the court set aside the award. The Contractors appealed
that judgment to the Court of Appeal, Abuja Judicial Division. On July&nbsp;22,
2016, the Court of Appeal upheld the decision of the lower court setting aside
the award. </font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">On
October&nbsp;21, 2016, the Contractors appealed the decision to the Supreme
Court of Nigeria. In June 2013, the Contractors filed a lawsuit against NNPC in
the Nige</font><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">rian federal high court in order to preserve
their ability to seek enforcement of the PSC in the courts if necessary. Following
dismissal by this court, the Contractors appealed to the Nigerian Court of
Appeal in June 2016. In October 2014, the Contractors filed suit in the United
States District Court for the Southern District of New York to enforce, if
necessary, the arbitration award against NNPC assets residing within that
jurisdiction. NNPC has moved to dismiss the lawsuit. At this time, the net
impact of this matter on the Corporation's consolidated financial results cannot
be reasonably estimated. However, regardless of the outcome of enforcement
proceedings, the Corporation does not expect the proceedings to have a material
effect upon the Corporation's operations or financial condition. </font></font><a name="XBRL_TS_f4348cf8394e4381bc24c5eaa_bclEnd"></a></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.25in;text-indent:-.25in;"><a name="XBRL_CS_d35276f1f5ee4a74a4a82ebbc"></a></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font style="border:none;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Derivative
Instruments.</font></b></font><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> The
Corporation&#8217;s size, strong capital structure, geographic diversity and the
complementary nature of the Upstream, Downstream and Chemical businesses reduce
the Corporation&#8217;s enterprise-wide risk from changes in commodity prices,
currency rates and interest rates. In addition, the Corporation uses
commodity-based contracts, including derivatives, to manage commodity price
risk and for trading purposes. <a name="XBRL_TS_06858e985f0f4634b5292d463"></a>Commodity
contracts held for trading purposes are presented in the Consolidated Statement
of Income on a net basis in the line &#8220;Sales and other operating revenue.&#8221; The
Corporation&#8217;s commodity derivatives are not accounted for under hedge
accounting.<a name="XBRL_TS_06858e985f0f4634b5292d463_bclEnd"></a> At
times, the Corporation also enters into forward currency and interest rate
derivatives, none of which are material to the Corporation&#8217;s financial position
as of March 31, 2019 and December 31, 2018, or results of operations for the
periods ended March 31, 2019 and 2018.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Credit risk associated with the
Corporation&#8217;s derivative position is mitigated by several factors, including
the use of derivative clearing exchanges and the quality of and financial
limits placed on derivative counterparties. The Corporation maintains a system
of controls that includes the authorization, reporting and monitoring of
derivative activity.</font></font><a name="XBRL_TS_e2b5c02bb5034eada1b281798_bclEnd"></a></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><a name="XBRL_TS_49ef50b89a54420a9d4227fcd"></a><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">At March 31, 2019, the net notional long/(short) position of
derivative instruments was (</font></font><a name="XBRL_CS_fa26daa2ae5744ea9b90f981d"></a><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">35</font></font><a name="XBRL_CS_fa26daa2ae5744ea9b90f981d_bclEnd"></a><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">) million barrels for crude oil, was (<a name="XBRL_CS_59192de8e4454c2ab0a72499f"></a>36<a name="XBRL_CS_59192de8e4454c2ab0a72499f_bclEnd"></a>) million barrels for
products, and was (<a name="XBRL_CS_c0ce9f29b3374a61ae4dec527"></a>10<a name="XBRL_CS_c0ce9f29b3374a61ae4dec527_bclEnd"></a>) million MMBtus of natural
gas. At December 31, 2018, the net notional long/(short) position of derivative
instruments was (<a name="XBRL_CS_c4c7c915ce92448cb343fce05"></a>19<a name="XBRL_CS_c4c7c915ce92448cb343fce05_bclEnd"></a>) million barrels for crude
oil and was (<a name="XBRL_CS_af8d57d565a541b19414a8a12"></a>9<a name="XBRL_CS_af8d57d565a541b19414a8a12_bclEnd"></a>) million barrels for
products.</font></font><a name="XBRL_TS_49ef50b89a54420a9d4227fcd_bclEnd"></a></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><a name="XBRL_TS_4fcf613c95464e8aa6c4cbb24"></a><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Realized and unrealized gains/(losses) on derivative instruments
that were recognized in the Consolidated Statement of Income are included in
the following lines on a before-tax basis:</font></font><a name="XBRL_TS_4fcf613c95464e8aa6c4cbb24_bclEnd"></a><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> &nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:31.5pt;margin-right:4.5pt;margin-top:3.0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-13.5pt;"><a name="XBRL_TS_8c633de41a1147aaa72078772"></a><a name="XBRL_TS_bfd44bdcbe5f41f69ac7726b0"></a><font style="border:none;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1) </font></i></font><a name="XBRL_FS_1fa59658f3cd49409d01c2f01"></a><font style="border:none;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenue is determined by primary country
of operations. Excludes certain sales and other operating revenues in Non&#8209;U.S.
operations where attribution to a specific country is not practicable.</font></i></font><a name="XBRL_FS_1fa59658f3cd49409d01c2f01_bclEnd"></a><a name="XBRL_TS_8c633de41a1147aaa72078772_bclEnd"></a><a name="XBRL_TS_bfd44bdcbe5f41f69ac7726b0_bclEnd"></a></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:10.0pt;"><a name="XBRL_TS_d37ad7d3d6074adf83d736967"></a></p>

<DIV bclHeader>


<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;mso-border-shadow:yes;mso-line-height-rule:exactly;mso-padding-alt:31.0pt 31.0pt 31.0pt 31.0pt;mso-pagination:widow-orphan no-line-numbers;"><font style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:.7pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>


</DIV>
<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:10.0pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:115%;">9. Leases</font></b></font><a name="XBRL_TS_d37ad7d3d6074adf83d736967_bclEnd"></a></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><a name="XBRL_TS_425971ea2824482bba4dc8dd3"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Corporation and its consolidated affiliates generally purchase
the property, plant and equipment used in operations, but there are situations
where assets are leased, primarily for drilling equipment, tankers, office
buildings, railcars, and other moveable equipment. </font></font><a name="XBRL_TS_9cc9b23f7bce47a98fcb0206e"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Right of use assets and lease liabilities are established on the
balance sheet for leases with an expected term greater than one year, by
discounting the amounts fixed in the lease agreement for the duration of the
lease which is reasonably certain, considering the probability of exercising
any early termination and extension options. The portion of the fixed payment
related to service costs for drilling equipment and tankers is excluded from
the calculation of right of use assets and lease liabilities.</font></font><a name="XBRL_TS_9cc9b23f7bce47a98fcb0206e_bclEnd"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> Generally assets are leased only for a
portion of their useful lives, and are accounted for as operating leases. In
limited situations assets are leased for nearly all of their useful lives, and
are accounted for as finance leases.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Variable payments under
these lease agreements are not significant. Residual value guarantees,
restrictions, or covenants related to leases, and transactions with related
parties are also not significant. <a name="XBRL_TS_12e5a25f590a468aa187708de"></a>In
general, leases are capitalized using the incremental borrowing rate of the
leasing affiliate.<a name="XBRL_TS_12e5a25f590a468aa187708de_bclEnd"></a> The
Corporation&#8217;s activities as a lessor are not significant.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">At adoption of the
lease accounting change (see Note 2), on January 1, 2019, an operating lease
liability of $3.3 billion was recorded and the operating lease right of use
asset was $4.3 billion, including $1.0 billion of previously recorded prepaid
leases. There was no cumulative earnings effect adjustment.</font></font><a name="XBRL_TS_425971ea2824482bba4dc8dd3_bclEnd"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

leases not yet commenced totaled $</font></font><a name="XBRL_CS_16dc5b10dceb423c9419a8ed7"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">2.6</font></font><a name="XBRL_CS_16dc5b10dceb423c9419a8ed7_bclEnd"></a><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> billion. Included
among these commitments is $<a name="XBRL_CS_ba42dab876ca4b3bbcb420c90"></a>1.7<a name="XBRL_CS_ba42dab876ca4b3bbcb420c90_bclEnd"></a> billion for crude oil
pipeline transportation that is expected to commence later in 2019. The
underlying assets for these leases were primarily designed by, and are being
constructed by, the lessors. These unrecorded lease commitments are the primary
difference between the operating lease liabilities reflected in the table above
and the $<a name="XBRL_CS_80976bde38da44069370e11af"></a>6.1<a name="XBRL_CS_80976bde38da44069370e11af_bclEnd"></a> billion disclosed at
December 31, 2018, for minimum lease commitments under the prior lease

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:.5in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">References in this
discussion to Corporate earnings mean net income attributable to ExxonMobil
(U.S. GAAP) from the consolidated income statement. Unless otherwise indicated,
references to earnings, Upstream, Downstream, Chemical and Corporate and financing
segment earnings, and earnings per share are ExxonMobil's share after excluding
amounts attributable to noncontrolling interests.</font></i></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:27.0pt;margin-right:.7in;margin-top:0in;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">REVIEW OF FIRST QUARTER 2019 RESULTS </font></b></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">ExxonMobil&#8217;s first quarter 2019 earnings were $2.4&nbsp;billion, or $0.55
per diluted share, compared with $4.7&nbsp;billion a year earlier. The decrease
in earnings was primarily the result of lower Downstream and Chemical margins
and higher scheduled maintenance activity.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Oil&#8209;equivalent production was 4.0&nbsp;million barrels per day, up
2&nbsp;percent from the prior year. Excluding entitlement effects and
divestments, oil&#8209;equivalent production was up 3 percent from the prior
year.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Corporation distributed $3.5&nbsp;billion in dividends to
shareholders.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Upstream earnings were $2,876&nbsp;million
in the first quarter of 2019, down $621&nbsp;million from the first quarter of
2018.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face=Symbol style="border:none;"><font face=Symbol lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
&nbsp;</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Realizations
decreased earnings by $30&nbsp;million due to lower liquids realizations of
$360 million, partly offset by higher gas realizations of $330 million.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face=Symbol style="border:none;"><font face=Symbol lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
&nbsp;</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Higher
volume and mix effects increased earnings by $80&nbsp;million due to higher
liquids volumes of $230 million, partly offset by lower gas volumes of $150
million.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face=Symbol style="border:none;"><font face=Symbol lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
&nbsp;</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">All
other items decreased earnings by $670 million due to the absence of a gain on
the Scarborough asset sale of $366&nbsp;million, higher growth-related expenses
and asset impairment charges.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face=Symbol style="border:none;"><font face=Symbol lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
&nbsp;</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">U.S.
Upstream earnings were $96&nbsp;million, down $333&nbsp;million from the prior
year quarter.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face=Symbol style="border:none;"><font face=Symbol lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
&nbsp;</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Non&#8209;U.S.
Upstream earnings were $2,780&nbsp;million, down $288&nbsp;million from the
prior year quarter.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face=Symbol style="border:none;"><font face=Symbol lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
&nbsp;</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">On
an oil&#8209;equivalent basis, production increased 2&nbsp;percent from the
first quarter of 2018.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face=Symbol style="border:none;"><font face=Symbol lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
&nbsp;</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Liquids
production totaled 2.3&nbsp;million barrels per day, up 111,000&nbsp;barrels
per day due to U.S. growth and improved reliability, partly offset by decline. </font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face=Symbol style="border:none;"><font face=Symbol lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
&nbsp;</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Natural
gas production was 9.9&nbsp;billion cubic feet per day, down 114&nbsp;million
cubic feet per day due to lower demand, decline and divestments, partly offset
by lower maintenance and growth.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Listed below are descriptions of ExxonMobil&#8217;s volumes
reconciliation factors which are provided to facilitate understanding of the
terms.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></i></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Entitlements - Net
Interest</font></i></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> are changes to ExxonMobil&#8217;s share of production volumes caused by
non-operational changes to volume-determining factors. These factors consist of
net interest changes specified in Production Sharing Contracts (PSCs) which
typically occur when cumulative investment returns or production volumes
achieve defined thresholds, changes in equity upon achieving pay-out in partner
investment carry situations, equity redeterminations as specified in venture
agreements, or as a result of the termination or expiry of a concession. Once a
net interest change has occurred, it typically will not be reversed by
subsequent events, such as lower crude oil prices.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:12.25pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Entitlements - Price,
Spend and Other</font></i></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> are changes to ExxonMobil&#8217;s share of production volumes resulting
from temporary changes to non-operational volume-determining factors. These
factors include changes in oil and gas prices or spending levels from one
period to another. According to the terms of contractual arrangements or
government royalty regimes, price or spending variability can increase or
decrease royalty burdens and/or volumes attributable to ExxonMobil. For
example, at higher prices, fewer barrels are required for ExxonMobil to recover
its costs. These effects generally vary from period to period with field
spending patterns or market prices for oil and natural gas. Such factors can
also include other temporary changes in net interest as dictated by specific
provisions in production agreements.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:12.25pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Quotas</font></i></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> are changes in
ExxonMobil&#8217;s allowable production arising from production constraints imposed
by countries which are members of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting
Countries (OPEC). Volumes reported in this category would have been readily
producible in the absence of the quota.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:12.25pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Divestments</font></i></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> are reductions in
ExxonMobil&#8217;s production arising from commercial arrangements to fully or
partially reduce equity in a field or asset in exchange for financial or other
economic consideration. </font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:12.25pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Growth and Other</font></i></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"> factors comprise all
other operational and non-operational factors not covered by the above
definitions that may affect volumes attributable to ExxonMobil. Such factors
include, but are not limited to, production enhancements from project and work
program activities, acquisitions including additions from asset exchanges,
downtime, market demand, natural field decline, and any fiscal or commercial
terms that do not affect entitlements.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Downstream earnings
were ($256)&nbsp;million in the first quarter of 2019, down $1,196&nbsp;million
from the first quarter of 2018.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face=Symbol style="border:none;"><font face=Symbol lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
&nbsp;</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Margins
decreased earnings by $860&nbsp;million.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face=Symbol style="border:none;"><font face=Symbol lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
&nbsp;</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Volume
and mix effects remained essentially flat due to higher scheduled maintenance,
offset by improved yield&nbsp;/&nbsp;sales mix impacts.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face=Symbol style="border:none;"><font face=Symbol lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
&nbsp;</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">All
other items decreased earnings by $340&nbsp;million due to higher scheduled
maintenance and unfavorable yield / sales mix impacts.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face=Symbol style="border:none;"><font face=Symbol lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
&nbsp;</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">U.S.
Downstream earnings were ($161)&nbsp;million, down $480&nbsp;million from the
prior year quarter.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face=Symbol style="border:none;"><font face=Symbol lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
&nbsp;</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Non&#8209;U.S.
Downstream earnings were ($95)&nbsp;million, down $716&nbsp;million from the
prior year quarter.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face=Symbol style="border:none;"><font face=Symbol lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
&nbsp;</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Petroleum
product sales of 5.4&nbsp;million barrels per day were 17,000&nbsp;barrels per
day lower than the prior year quarter.</font></font></p>

  </td>
 <td nowrap valign=top width=3% style="height:12.0pt;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;">
  <p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=black face="Times New Roman,serif" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Chemical earnings of $518&nbsp;million in the first quarter
of 2019 were $493&nbsp;million lower than the first quarter of 2018.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.5in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face=Symbol style="border:none;"><font face=Symbol lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
&nbsp;</font></font><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Lower margins
decreased earnings by $360&nbsp;million.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.5in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face=Symbol style="border:none;"><font face=Symbol lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
&nbsp;</font></font><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Volume and mix effects
increased earnings by $60&nbsp;million.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.5in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face=Symbol style="border:none;"><font face=Symbol lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
&nbsp;</font></font><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">All other items
decreased earnings by $190&nbsp;million, mainly due to higher growth-related
expenses and unfavorable foreign exchange impacts.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face=Symbol style="border:none;"><font face=Symbol lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
&nbsp;</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">U.S.
Chemical earnings were $161&nbsp;million, down $342&nbsp;million from the prior
year quarter.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin-bottom:0in;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face=Symbol style="border:none;"><font face=Symbol lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
&nbsp;</font></font><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Non&#8209;U.S.
Chemical earnings were $357&nbsp;million, down $151&nbsp;million from the prior
year quarter.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.5in;text-align:justify;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face=Symbol style="border:none;"><font face=Symbol lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
&nbsp;</font></font><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">First quarter prime
product sales of 6.8&nbsp;million metric tons were 104,000&nbsp;metric tons
higher than the prior year quarter due to growth.</font></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;"><br>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:.5in;margin-top:0in;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Because of the ongoing
nature of our asset management and divestment program, we believe it is useful
for investors to consider proceeds associated with asset sales together with
cash provided by operating activities when evaluating cash available for
investment in the business and financing activities, including shareholder
distributions.</font></i></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash flow from
operations and asset sales in the first quarter of 2019 was $8.4 billion,
including asset sales of $0.1 billion, a decrease of $1.5 billion from the
comparable 2018 period primarily reflecting lower asset sale proceeds.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash provided by
operating activities totaled $8.3 billion for the first three months of 2019, $0.2
billion lower than 2018. The major source of funds was net income including
noncontrolling interests of $2.4 billion, a decrease of $2.4 billion from the
prior year period. The adjustment for the noncash provision of $4.6 billion for
depreciation and depletion was up $0.1 billion from 2018. Changes in
operational working capital contributed $2.3 billion, up $1.9 billion from the
prior year period. All other items net decreased cash flows by $0.9 billion in
2019 versus a reduction of $1.1 billion in 2018. See the Condensed Consolidated
Statement of Cash Flows for additional details. </font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Investing activities
for the first three months of 2019 used net cash of $5.8 billion, an increase
of $3.9 billion compared to the prior year. Spending for additions to property,
plant and equipment of $5.2 billion was $1.9 billion higher than 2018. Proceeds
from asset sales of $0.1 billion decreased $1.3 billion. Investments and
advances increased $0.8 billion to $0.9 billion.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Net cash used by
financing activities was $1.0 billion in the first three months of 2019, a
decrease of $4.7 billion from 2018. The net addition to short-term debt was
$3.0 billion compared to a net reduction of $1.9 billion in 2018. </font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the first three
months of 2019, Exxon Mobil Corporation purchased 5 million shares of its
common stock for the treasury at a gross cost of $0.4 billion. These purchases
were made to offset shares or units settled in shares issued in conjunction
with the company&#8217;s benefit plans and programs. Shares outstanding decreased
from 4,237 million at year-end to 4,231 million at the end of the first quarter
of 2019. Purchases may be made both in the open market and through negotiated
transactions, and may be increased, decreased or discontinued at any time
without prior notice.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Corporation
distributed a total of $3.5 billion to shareholders in the first quarter of 2019
through dividends. </font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Total cash and cash
equivalents of $4.6 billion at the end of the first quarter of 2019 compared to
$3.0 billion at year-end 2018.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Total debt at the end
of the first quarter of 2019 was $40.8 billion compared to $37.8 billion at
year-end 2018. The Corporation's debt to total capital ratio was 17.1 percent
at the end of the first quarter of 2019 compared to 16.0 percent at year-end
2018.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Corporation has access to significant capacity of long-term
and short-term liquidity. Internally generated funds are generally expected to
cover financial requirements, supplemented by short-term and long-term debt as
required.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Corporation, as
part of its ongoing asset management program, continues to evaluate its mix of
assets for potential upgrade. Because of the ongoing nature of this program,
dispositions will continue to be made from time to time which will result in
either gains or losses. Additionally, the Corporation continues to evaluate
opportunities to enhance its business portfolio through acquisitions of assets
or companies, and enters into such transactions from time to time. Key criteria
for evaluating acquisitions include potential for future growth and attractive
current valuations. Acquisitions may be made with cash, shares of the
Corporation&#8217;s common stock, or both.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Litigation and other
contingencies are discussed in Note 3 to the unaudited condensed consolidated
financial statements.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:13.5pt;margin-right:.25in;margin-top:3.0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-13.5pt;"><a name="XBRL_TS_6cefe939bbe2465bafbbbbc17"></a><a name="XBRL_TS_1265fdb9ebe245b2b1af566f4"></a><a name="Xbrl_Tag12"></a><a name="Xbrl_Tag2"></a><font style="border:none;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1) </font></i></font><a name="Xbrl_Tag12_bclEnd"></a><a name="Xbrl_Tag2_bclEnd"></a><a name="XBRL_TS_1265fdb9ebe245b2b1af566f4_bclEnd"></a><a name="XBRL_TS_6cefe939bbe2465bafbbbbc17_bclEnd"></a><font style="border:none;"><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Includes &#8220;Other taxes and duties&#8221; plus taxes that are
included in &#8220;Production and manufacturing expenses&#8221; and &#8220;Selling, general and
administrative expenses.&#8221;</font></i></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Total taxes were $10.0 billion for the first quarter of 2019,
a decrease of $1.3 billion from 2018. Income tax expense decreased by $0.6
billion to $1.9 billion reflecting lower pre-tax income. The effective income
tax rate was 53 percent compared to 40 percent in the prior year period. This
increase mainly reflects a higher share of earnings in higher tax jurisdictions
in the Non-U.S. Upstream segment. Total other taxes and duties decreased by $0.7
billion to $8.1 billion.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the United States, the Corporation has various ongoing
U.S. federal income tax positions at issue with the Internal Revenue Service
(IRS) for tax years beginning in 2006. The IRS has asserted penalties
associated with several of those positions. The Corporation has not recognized
the penalties as an expense because the Corporation does not expect the
penalties to be sustained under applicable law. The Corporation has filed a
refund suit for tax years 2006-2009 in a U.S. federal district court with
respect to the positions at issue for those years. Unfavorable resolution of
all positions at issue with the IRS would not have a materially adverse effect
on the Corporation&#8217;s net income or liquidity.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">RECENTLY ISSUED ACCOUNTING STANDARDS</font></b></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font style="border:none;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><a name=BookmarkName1></a><font style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Effective January
1, 2020, ExxonMobil will adopt the Financial Accounting Standards Board&#8217;s
update, </font><i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financial Instruments &#8211; Credit Losses (Topic 326)</font></i><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">, as amended.
The standard requires a valuation allowance for credit losses be recognized for
certain financial assets that reflects the current expected credit loss over
the asset&#8217;s contractual life. The valuation allowance considers the risk of
loss, even if remote, and considers past events, current conditions and
expectations of the future. The Corporation is evaluating the standard and its
effect on the Corporation&#8217;s financial statements.</font></font><a name="BookmarkName1_bclEnd"></a></p>

</DIV>
<p align=center style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-right:31.5pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">PART II.&#160; OTHER
INFORMATION</font></b></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-right:31.5pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-right:31.5pt;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Item 1.&#160; Legal
Proceedings</font></b></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-right:31.5pt;"><font face=Arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">On March 20, 2019, the
State of California Air Resources Board (CARB) informed ExxonMobil Oil
Corporation (EMOC) of its intention to attempt to settle an enforcement matter
involving the formerly owned Torrance Refinery in California under the
California Health and Safety Code. Specifically, CARB contends that the
refinery failed to timely calibrate and inspect a greenhouse gas reporting
meter as required by the applicable regulations and to accurately report
greenhouse gas emissions from refinery operations in 2014 and 2015 in a manner
consistent with applicable regulations. The alleged violations have been
corrected, but CARB is seeking penalties in excess of $100,000 to resolve the
matter. EMOC is in settlement discussions with CARB, and the parties have entered
into a tolling agreement to facilitate settlement discussions.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">In a matter last
reported in the Corporation&#8217;s Form 10-Q for first quarter of 2017, the U.S.
Department of Justice (DOJ) and U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)
filed a complaint and proposed consent decree on March 6, 2019, to settle a
pending enforcement action with EMOC regarding alleged violations at EMOC&#8217;s
Beaumont Refinery in Texas under the Clean Air Act and various sections of the
EPA&#8217;s Chemical Accident Prevention Provisions. The DOJ and EPA had contended
that EMOC failed to identify hazards, failed to design and maintain a safe
facility, and failed to mitigate the consequences of a claimed accidental
release related to a flash fire that occurred on April 17, 2013. Additionally,
based on an on-site inspection in 2013, the DOJ and EPA claim that EMOC failed
to include all covered processes in its risk management program and failed to
inspect certain process equipment in a timely fashion. Pending approval by the
U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Texas, Beaumont Division, the
parties have agreed to a civil penalty of $616,000, payment of $730,000 to a
Supplemental Environmental Project, and additional corrective actions to
resolve the matter.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">As most recently
reported in the Corporation&#8217;s Form 10-Q for the second quarter of 2014, the DOJ
contacted ExxonMobil Pipeline Company (EMPCo) concerning possible civil charges
under the Clean Water Act arising in connection with the July 1, 2011,
discharge of crude oil into the Yellowstone River from EMPCo&#8217;s Silvertip
Pipeline near Laurel, Montana. In March 2019, EMPCo reached an agreement with
the DOJ on a Consent Decree to resolve the matter. The Consent Decree, once
entered by the U.S. District Court in the District of Montana, will require
EMPCo to pay a civil penalty to the United States in the amount of $1.05
million.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">As last reported in the
Corporation&#8217;s 2018 Form 10-K, on July 20, 2017, the United States Department of
Treasury, Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) assessed a civil penalty
against Exxon Mobil Corporation, ExxonMobil Development Company and ExxonMobil
Oil Corporation for violating the Ukraine-Related Sanctions Regulations, 31
C.F.R. part 589. The assessed civil penalty is in the amount of $2,000,000.
ExxonMobil and its affiliates have been and continue to be in compliance with
all sanctions and disagree that any violation has occurred. ExxonMobil and its
affiliates filed a complaint on July&nbsp;20, 2017, in the United States
Federal District Court, Northern District of Texas seeking judicial review of,
and to enjoin, the civil penalty under the Administrative Procedures Act and
the United States Constitution, including on the basis that it represents an
arbitrary and capricious action by OFAC and a violation of the Company&#8217;s due
process rights.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Refer to the relevant
portions of Note 3 of this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for further
information on legal proceedings.</font></font></p>

<p style="border:none;margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:justify;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;">Note 1 - On August 1,
2000, the Corporation announced its intention to resume purchases of shares of
its common stock for the treasury both to offset shares issued in conjunction
with company benefit plans and programs and to gradually reduce the number of
shares outstanding. The announcement did not specify an amount or expiration
date. The Corporation has continued to purchase shares since this announcement
and to report purchased volumes in its quarterly earnings releases. In its
earnings release dated February 2, 2016, the Corporation stated it will
continue to acquire shares to offset dilution in conjunction with benefit plans
and programs, but had suspended making purchases to reduce shares outstanding
effective beginning the first quarter of 2016.</font></font></p>

<p align=center style="border:none;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></b></font></p>

W. Woods</font></b></font></p>

<p align=center style="border:none;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><b><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">Pursuant to Securities

<p style="border:none;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" style="border:none;"><font face="Times New Roman,serif" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>
